data.long_meaning: A name of Arabic and Urdu origin meaning 'protector', 'defender' and 'rare'. Derived from the Arabic word 'rakhasa' meaning 'to protect'. The name Rakhas carries the meaning “Protector, Defender” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu. Parents who choose Rakhas usually hope their child will grow to embody protector, defender and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rakhas total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Rakhas" carries significant cultural importance in the Islamic world due to its meaning of 'protector'. In Islamic tradition, the belief in divine providence and the idea that remembrance of Allah serves as protection is deeply ingrained. Naming a child "Rakhas" invokes the idea of a guardian and protector, whether it refers to the parents or the belief in Allah as the ultimate protector and guardian of faiths.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Rakhas" lies in its association with the concept of shield and protection in Islamic tradition. The verse in the Quran (Surah Al-Baqarah, 286) states, "And when I am angered, much will be sin in me." This verse highlights the concept of seeking Allah's protection against His anger and punishment through repentance and devotion. Thus, the name "Rakhas", meaning 'protector' or 'defender', is a powerful reminder of the significance of seeking Allah's protection, both from this world's afflictions and the permanent isolation from His Mercy in the hereafter. May Allah protect us all.
